topic.title: Proposed NFSA Amendment for AAY Households

subtopics.title: Proposed AAY Entitlement Change
subtopics.summary: The Union Government has proposed amending Section 3(1) of the National Food Security Act 2013 to change foodgrain entitlement for Antyodaya Anna Yojana households. The current rule gives each AAY household a fixed 35 kg per month irrespective of family size. The proposal shifts the basis to individuals, at 7 kg per person per month, with a maximum of 35 kg per household.
facts: Amendment seeks to modify Section 3(1) of NFSA 2013 relating to AAY foodgrain entitlement
Current provision: every AAY household receives 35 kg per month irrespective of family size
Proposed provision: every individual in an AAY household receives 7 kg per month
Proposed ceiling: maximum 35 kg per household
The proposal moves the basis of AAY entitlement from household to individual
The proposal has been made by the Union Government

subtopics.title: Rationale and Limits of the Amendment
subtopics.summary: The Union Government argues that the household-based AAY entitlement creates inequities within the category. Small households receive more foodgrain per person than larger ones, and the amendment would make distribution proportional to household size. The government also says the change reduces disparities with Priority Household beneficiaries, but the amendment does not address inclusion errors.
facts: Government argues the household-based entitlement creates inequities within the AAY category
Per capita inequality: small households receive more foodgrain per person than larger households
Better equity: distribution becomes proportional to household size
Rationalisation: allocation aligned more closely with nutritional requirements
Uniformity: reduces disparities between AAY and Priority Household beneficiaries
Limitation: the amendment does not address inclusion errors, where ineligible beneficiaries continue to receive NFSA benefits

subtopics.title: NFSA 2013 and Beneficiary Categories
subtopics.summary: The National Food Security Act 2013 was enacted to ensure food and nutritional security through subsidised foodgrains under the Targeted Public Distribution System. It made foodgrain access a legal right for two-thirds of the population. AAY households get 35 kg per month and PHH households get 5 kg per person per month at subsidised rates.
facts: NFSA 2013 was enacted to ensure food and nutritional security
It provides subsidised foodgrains through the Targeted Public Distribution System
It made foodgrain access a legal right for two-thirds of the population
AAY is meant for the poorest of the poor households
AAY families get 35 kg per month, fixed per household
PHH covers other eligible households
PHH get 5 kg per person per month
AAY entitlement is fixed per household; PHH entitlement is per person

subtopics.title: PDS Background and PMGKAY
subtopics.summary: The Public Distribution System was introduced by the British during World War II, after the 1942-43 Bengal famine, to control food prices and ration foodgrains. It was initially focused on urban food security and expanded to tribal and poor areas after the Green Revolution. PMGKAY (2020) added extra free foodgrains for NFSA beneficiaries.
facts: PDS in India was introduced by the British during World War II
It was introduced after the 1942-43 Bengal famine to control food prices and ration foodgrains
Initially focused on urban food security
Expanded to tribal and poor areas after the Green Revolution in the 1970s and 1980s
Essential goods distributed: wheat, sugar, rice and kerosene
Administered by the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution
RPDS (1992) aims to extend PDS access to remote, hilly areas through an area-based approach
PMGKAY (2020) provided an extra 5 kg of free foodgrains to AAY and PHH beneficiaries
PMGKAY covered 81.35 crore people alongside regular PDS entitlements
Kerala set up one of India's earliest PDS in 1962; Tamil Nadu introduced universal free rice distribution in 2011

quizzes.title: AAY Amendment Recall
quizzes.passage: The Union Government has proposed an amendment to the National Food Security Act, 2013, that would change how foodgrains are allocated to households under the Antyodaya Anna Yojana. At present, each AAY household receives a fixed quantity of foodgrain each month, no matter how many members it has. The government argues that this household-based system creates inequities within the AAY category, because small households end up receiving more foodgrain per person than larger households. Under the proposal, the entitlement would be worked out for each individual in the household, with an overall ceiling for each household. The government expects this to make distribution more proportional to household size and to align allocation more closely with nutritional requirements. The change would also reduce disparities between AAY households and Priority Households. The amendment, however, does not deal with every problem in the system, because inclusion errors remain. The National Food Security Act was enacted to ensure food and nutritional security through subsidised foodgrains delivered by a targeted system. The proposal is still under consideration and is discussed here as a change in the making.

questions.q: Which Section of the National Food Security Act 2013 does the proposed amendment seek to modify?
questions.explanation: The amendment seeks to modify Section 3(1) of the NFSA relating to AAY foodgrain entitlement.

questions.q: Under the proposed amendment, how much foodgrain does each individual in an AAY household receive per month?
questions.explanation: The proposal gives every individual in an AAY household 7 kg per month, subject to a household maximum of 35 kg.

questions.q: What is the maximum foodgrain entitlement cap per AAY household per month under the proposed amendment?
questions.explanation: The proposal keeps a maximum of 35 kg per household per month, while each individual receives 7 kg.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The proposal would reduce disparities between AAY and PHH beneficiaries.
Reason (R): Under NFSA 2013, PHH beneficiaries receive 5 kg of foodgrain per person per month.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The PHH entitlement of 5 kg per person is a true fact but does not explain why the proposal reduces disparities.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Individual entitlement under the proposal (AAY)   ->   A. 7 kg per individual per month
II. Household ceiling under the proposal   ->   B. 35 kg per household per month
III. PHH entitlement under NFSA 2013   ->   C. 5 kg per person per month
IV. Year PMGKAY was launched   ->   D. 2020
questions.explanation: The proposal gives 7 kg per individual (I-A), the household ceiling is 35 kg (II-B), PHH get 5 kg per person (III-C), and PMGKAY was launched in 2020 (IV-D).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the proposed NFSA amendment:
I. It seeks to modify the entitlement under Section 3(1) for AAY households.
II. It addresses inclusion errors where ineligible beneficiaries receive NFSA benefits.
III. It would make distribution proportional to household size.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct because the amendment modifies Section 3(1), and III is correct, while II is wrong because inclusion errors are not addressed.

questions.q:
How many of the following statements about the proposed NFSA amendment are correct?
I. It seeks to modify Section 3(1) of the NFSA 2013.
II. The proposed AAY ceiling is 50 kg per household per month.
III. Per capita inequality is cited as a reason for the change.
IV. Priority Household beneficiaries currently receive 5 kg per person per month.
questions.explanation: Statements I, III and IV are correct, while II is wrong because the proposed ceiling is 35 kg per household.

questions.q: Under the current NFSA 2013 arrangement, how much foodgrain does every AAY household receive per month, irrespective of family size?
questions.explanation: Every AAY household currently receives 35 kg per month irrespective of family size, which the proposal would replace with a per-individual rate.

quizzes.title: Rationale and Limits Check
quizzes.passage: Foodgrain entitlements under the National Food Security Act are linked to categories of beneficiaries. Within the Antyodaya Anna Yojana, the present design gives a single fixed amount to each household, so the amount a person gets depends on how many people share the household. The Union Government has argued that this design produces inequities inside the category. A revised design would calculate the entitlement for each individual, while keeping a ceiling for each household so that large families do not receive unlimited grain. The government expects this to link allocation more closely with what people need to eat, and to make treatment across categories more uniform. The proposal does not, however, tackle one important concern in the system. Readers should remember that the amendment is still a proposal under discussion, and that its aims and limits are described in the booklet. The discussion covers the logic of the change, the effect on different households, and the parts of the system that remain unchanged. The rules discussed here are a useful base for answering questions on this theme.

questions.q: What term describes the concern the proposal does not tackle, where ineligible beneficiaries continue to receive NFSA benefits? (two words)
questions.explanation: The amendment does not address inclusion errors, where ineligible beneficiaries continue to receive NFSA benefits.

questions.q: Under the revised design, distribution would become proportional to what? (two words)
questions.explanation: The amendment would make distribution proportional to household size.

questions.q: The government expects the revised design to align allocation more closely with which requirements? (two words)
questions.explanation: Rationalisation aligns foodgrain allocation more closely with nutritional requirements.

questions.q: What term describes small households receiving more foodgrain per person than larger households? (three words)
questions.explanation: Per capita inequality is the term for small households receiving more foodgrain per person than larger households.

questions.q: The amendment aims to reduce disparities between AAY and which other beneficiary category? (short name)
questions.explanation: Uniformity reduces disparities between AAY and Priority Household beneficiaries.

questions.q: How many kg per month would each individual in an AAY household receive under the proposal? (in kg)
questions.explanation: The proposal gives each individual in an AAY household 7 kg per month.

questions.q: Which Section of the NFSA 2013 does the amendment modify? (in the form 3(x))
questions.explanation: The amendment seeks to modify Section 3(1) of the NFSA relating to AAY foodgrain entitlement.
